name: sk-scope-switch
description: Switch the active Sidekicks scope (active project/service in .sidekicks/settings.json) so your edits, new files, and downstream skills land in the right working folder — a service's src/. Use it whenever the user wants to start or move work into a particular project or service, OR hands you a file path that tells you which scope the work belongs to. Trigger when the user NAMES a target to work in — "switch me to the api service", "work on the auth service", "point my skills at X", "jump into project foo", "get me set up in X", "I'm in the wrong scope", "everything I write lands in the wrong place", "take me back to root" — even if they never say "switch" or "scope" and just name the project/service they want to operate in. ALSO — and this is the easy-to-miss case — trigger when the user hands over a PATH under projects/<project>/services/<service>/..., such as "implement projects/foo/services/api/src/docs/plan.md", "take a look at projects/foo/services/auth/src/handlers/login.go", "build out the spec at <path>", or just pastes such a path: infer the project and service from the path segments and align the active scope to them BEFORE touching the file, even though the user only asked you to work on the file and never mentioned scope or switching. ALSO trigger proactively when correct scope is a precondition for another task — before running a dev/PRD/review workflow on a story or spec whose path lives under a service, switch scope to that path first so the downstream skill writes to the right place. Do NOT trigger for: creating, adding, or removing a project or service; switching a service's git branch or syncing it to git (those are service checkout / service sync); editing a file whose path already resolves to the current active scope (no switch needed); or "where am I" / "what's my active project" / "what commands exist" questions (those are sk-hello and sk-cli).
